summary: A building contractor, developer or construction firm: completed and ongoing projects with their progress, the services and sectors it builds for, safety record, how it runs a site, the people, and a tender or project enquiry.

pages.purpose: Show scale and reliability: what the firm builds, live and finished projects, safety and how to send a project or tender enquiry.

sections.purpose: A huge signage-style headline beside a real site photo, with a small live board of current sites and their progress.
fields: Current sites with name and percent complete
sections.notes: The site board is a short list of ongoing projects with progress bars (build from hero + progress). A thin hazard-tape rule (accent and ink stripes) can separate the hero; it is decorative and its motion stops under reduced motion.

sections.purpose: Scale in a few figures: years, area built, projects delivered, safety record.
fields: Three or four figures with label
Source or as-of date for safety figures

sections.purpose: Featured projects as cards with status, type and place, linking to all projects.
alternatives: gallery-section: photo-led grid of finished buildings

sections.purpose: What the firm builds and offers (residential, commercial, public tender, renovation, design and build).
The safety record and approach, with certifications.
fields: Certifications (e.g. management system standards) with issuer

sections.purpose: How a site is run: a few concrete promises (reporting, cleanliness, schedule, neighbours).
fields: Three to five promises or stages with title and sentence

sections.purpose: Directors and site leads.
What clients and employers say, with their logos if permitted.
alternatives: logo-strip: a list of public and private employers

sections.purpose: Questions about tenders, contracts, warranties and timing.
Project or tender enquiry with type, budget band and site details.
Offices and yards with hours.
fields: Each office: address, phone, hours, map
sections.notes: Branches variant for more than one office.

pages.purpose: Every project, filterable by status and type.

sections.purpose: Title, breadcrumb and a line on the portfolio.
Status and type toggles with a live count over the project cards.
fields: Every project: name, place, type, status, client, value band, area, photo, summary
sections.notes: Count in a polite live region; empty state offers to clear filters.

pages.purpose: One project with facts and its progress over time.

sections.purpose: Name, place, status and a photo.
Key facts: client, value band, area, dates, type.
Drag through the build month by month: planned phases fill against the site diary; months after today show as a hatched forecast.
alternatives: activity-timeline: a simple diary of milestones
fields: Phases with name, planned start and end
Site diary entries with date and text
sections.notes: A month slider with previous / next / today buttons drives the Gantt and the diary quote; the read-out and diary are polite live regions; the month must be reachable by arrow keys and buttons, not only by dragging.

sections.purpose: Site and finished photos.
fields: Photos with alt text and date

sections.purpose: Two other projects to continue browsing.

pages.purpose: Each service or sector in more detail.

sections.purpose: Title and lead.
Services with scope and example projects.
Ask for a site visit or tender documents.
Project or tender enquiry.
Offices and hours.

content: Projects: name, place, type, status, client (with permission), value band, area, dates, summary, photos
Phase plans and site diary entries for ongoing projects (for the progress timeline)
Safety record with period and source, and certifications with issuer
How the firm runs a site: concrete promises
Directors and site leads with qualifications and portraits
Client quotes and employer logos with permission
Project types and budget bands for the enquiry form
Offices and yards: addresses, hours, phones
Company registration, contractor licence or classification details for the footer

styles.name: site hoarding
styles.why: Concrete grey with amber, tall condensed signage capitals for headlines, mono for dates and figures, a faint concrete-grain background; unhurried motion (headline wipe, one scroll drift, bars pouring in).

styles.name: engineering dark
styles.why: An engineering or infrastructure firm that wants a technical, dense, report-like look.

pitfalls: Safety figures without period and source, or certifications that have expired.
Naming clients or showing their logos without permission, especially on public tenders with disclosure rules.
Progress timelines left stale; if the diary is not updated, hide the timeline rather than show old progress as current.
Draggable timelines that only work with a mouse; provide buttons and arrow keys.
Hazard-tape and pouring animations that ignore reduced motion.
Photos of other firms' buildings or generic stock cranes; use the firm's own sites.
Missing contractor registration or licence details where the market requires them.
